title: Eight nodes, fanout one
request:
a rumour starting at node 0 in a cluster of eight, told to one peer a round

./your_program.sh gossip
init 8 1
round
round
round
infected
note: Three rounds for eight nodes, and it would be ten for a thousand. That growth is the whole reason gossip is used for cluster-wide state: the round count barely notices the cluster getting bigger.

title: What a wider fanout costs
request:
the same thirty-two nodes converged at fanout one and at fanout four

./your_program.sh gossip
init 32 1
converge
init 32 4
converge
note: Two rounds saved for four times the traffic. The fanout is not a free tuning knob: past a point the extra copies land on nodes that already knew, and the message count keeps climbing while the round count stops falling.
